verification_report.summary: Every proof item and displayed formula was checked sequentially under the accepted inputs. All new mathematical deductions pass; one incorrect external attribution prevents a strict 'correct' verdict. For arbitrary smooth real theta, local domination by dd^c rho, the compact connected fiber maximum principle, local sections, and product-coordinate positivity tests establish the descent bijection without closedness. Entire pole fibers are allowed, while an open set of pole fibers would contradict genuineness. The metric identification and pi_*dV=sigma^(n-1) give equality of possibly infinite exp(-mv) section norms, hence the multiplier-ideal section isometry, kernel identities and bounded graded-algebra identification without ideal base change. The k=0 case consists of constant potentials and is consistent. The fiber-integral construction defines a Borel measure, reflects equality by pushforward, and multiplies total mass by two. Local bounded BT approximation and the separate smooth zeta factor justify the nonclosed expansion: the horizontal n-th power and every term containing zeta squared vanish, leaving n*pi*((sigma+dd^c v)^(n-1)) wedge zeta. Exact pullback of truncations and indicators, locality and monotone convergence establish the unbounded extended identity, including zero mass on pole fibers. Bounded base Stokes gives mass 1, so upstairs extended mass is at most 2n and equals 2n for bounded potentials; the closed k-alpha top product is zero. The reduced equation has exactly the density (c/(2n))*f, with c=2n/integral(f sigma^(n-1)). Its normalized density satisfies all compact Kähler Lp hypotheses, and base uniqueness transfers to the specified bounded descended class. Smooth positive densities satisfy the standard smooth Kähler theorem's hypotheses. The exponential calculation asserts only a measure identity, and no arbitrary fiber-dependent solvability or uniqueness is claimed. For the toric model, the coefficient matrix F_ij/(z_i conjugate(z_j)) gives the Hessian criterion; translation yields sum F_i=k and D^2F*1=0. The compact-base bound and supporting-plane argument give nonnegative gradient coordinates. Strict base positivity gives a positive Hessian on sum x_i=0, strictly positive gradient coordinates, and coercivity of F-p dot x for every interior simplex point, proving the quotient bijection. The n>=2 and k>0 restrictions are correctly used. The Hopf-threefold comparison agrees with the established geometry and [Xia–Zhang](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21053). No BMP, global smooth regularization, or Hermitian cohomological mass identity is used. The sole defect concerns where the valid Lp continuity theorem is cited.

critical_errors.location: A reduced Monge–Ampere equation — citation of SGPT for continuous Lp solvability
critical_errors.issue: The sentence 'The usual compact Kähler Lp theorem in SGPT therefore gives a continuous solution v' attributes a regularity theorem to the wrong supplied source. The supplied SGPT author/chapter_envelopes.tex, thm:Yau_rel (lines 1021–1028), states existence and normalized uniqueness in the full-mass class E(X,theta;phi) for a non-pluripolar measure of prescribed total mass; it does not state Lp boundedness or continuity, and the source contains no matching Lp regularity theorem. Full mass does not by definition mean bounded or continuous. The standard compact Kähler Lp theorem explicitly allowed in the verification statement is valid and applies here, but its claimed location in SGPT is incorrect. This is a reference error, not a counterexample to the equation or its normalization.

repair_hints: Replace the attribution of continuous Lp solvability to SGPT by an explicit reference to the standard compact Kähler Lp theorem, for example [Kołodziej, introduction and Theorem 2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0611051), which records continuous existence and proves Hölder regularity. State the specialization B=P^(n-1), density g=f/I, I=integral f sigma^(n-1)>0, integral g sigma^(n-1)=1, and uniqueness modulo constants. Kołodziej's dd^c=2i partial bar-partial is converted to this chapter's dd^c=i partial bar-partial/(2pi) by v=4pi*u_source; the current and density remain unchanged. SGPT thm:Yau_rel can still support full-mass existence/uniqueness, but should not be presented as the missing regularity statement. This citation correction requires no change to the reduction formulas.
